requirements.text: Office Printing service is being retired
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_041' AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: service resolved from the seed by name: 'Office Printing' is SVC_041 (ORG_001, status repair_in_progress), the only service with 'print' in its name or description
retired is the seed's status value for a retired service (six services carry it)

requirements.text: All printer-related offerings under this service are no longer supported
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_050' AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: SVCOFF_050 'Print Server - HQ' is the only offering with business_service = SVC_041 on the seed, and the only offering named for printing, so 'all printer-related offerings' is this one row
'no longer supported' read as status retired, kept from the benchmark check; the offering follows its retired service

disagreement: form: A anchors SVCOFF_050 by id, B selects business_service = 'SVC_041' with expected 1; kept A's because it names the benchmark's row and the one offering under the service, so both count the same row

requirements.text: offerings under this service are no longer supported (close the open incidents raised against them)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_015' AND status = 'closed' AND close_notes IS NOT NULL AND resolution_code IS NOT NULL AND resolution_notes IS NOT NULL
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: an unsupported offering cannot keep open incidents, and list_incidents and update_incident are in the tools
INC_015 'Reception Printer Offline' is one of the two incidents on SVCOFF_050 not yet resolved or closed (status new on the seed); INC_003 and INC_089 on the same offering are already resolved
close_notes IS NOT NULL kept from the benchmark check; its wording is not fixed

policy 3.3 reaches closed only through resolved, and resolved requires resolution_code and resolution_notes, so both must be set; resolution_code is tested as IS NOT NULL, not against the policy's enumeration, because the seed uses values outside it ('Solution Provided')

disagreement: cells: A tests status and close_notes only (the benchmark's cells), B adds resolution_code IS NOT NULL and resolution_notes IS NOT NULL; chose B's because policy 3.3 makes them a precondition of closed and the tighter correct predicate is kept

requirements.text: offerings under this service are no longer supported (boundary: incidents on the service with no offering are not swept in)
requirements.selector: service = 'SVC_041' AND service_offering IS NULL AND status NOT IN ('resolved', 'closed')
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE service = 'SVC_041' AND service_offering IS NULL AND status NOT IN ('resolved', 'closed')
assumptions: the request scopes the loss of support to the printer offerings; the seven open incidents filed against the service with no offering (laptop, tablet and dock issues such as INC_079 'Laptop Fan') are the rows a loose 'close everything on the retired service' reading would sweep in, and must stay open
disagreement: form: A's status predicate is NOT IN ('resolved', 'closed'), B's is IN ('new', 'in_progress', 'on_hold'); equivalent under the policy's enumeration and both count 7; kept A's

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the four benchmark checks (all kept), the retirement of SVC_041 and SVCOFF_050, the closure of INC_015 and INC_064 as the step the request implies, and the stay on the seven open incidents of SVC_041 that have no offering; they differ on the cells of the two closures and in form elsewhere.
disagreement: value: cells of the INC_015 and INC_064 closures: A tests status = closed and close_notes IS NOT NULL (the benchmark's cells), B adds resolution_code IS NOT NULL and resolution_notes IS NOT NULL; kept B's because policy 3.3 reaches closed only through resolved, which requires both fields, so B's predicate is right and tighter. An agent that sets closed with close_notes alone passes the benchmark but not this file (logged on each requirement).
disagreement: form: the offering requirement: A anchors SVCOFF_050 by id, B selects by business_service = 'SVC_041' with expected 1; kept A's, the benchmark's row and the only offering under the service; the two give the same verdict on the seed.
disagreement: form: the stay's status predicate: A NOT IN ('resolved', 'closed'), B IN ('new', 'in_progress', 'on_hold'); equivalent under the policy's enumeration; kept A's.
The request never says to close incidents; the two incident checks are kept as the step it implies (list_incidents and update_incident are in the tools). The two resolved incidents on SVCOFF_050 (INC_003, INC_089) carry no stay: resolved -> closed is a valid transition and the request fixes them neither way. The seed's resolution_code values ('Solution Provided', 'No resolution provided') lie outside the policy's enumeration, so resolution_code is tested as IS NOT NULL only. The acting user is an admin, so no role check applies.
